summary: 小说《慢的发现》借极地探险家约翰·富兰克林的生平，把“慢”写成感知、思考和行动的方式。书评把历史人物和小说塑造相对照，并分析这种写法如何进入作品语言。
logic: 小说赋予人物缓慢的感知
考察缓慢与极地探险的关系
分析语言风格与读者反响

paragraphs.brief: 为寻航道踏上首次北极远征
sentences: The English explorer and writer John Franklin (1786–1847) joined the Navy at the age of 14, and fought at the battle of Trafalgar.
英国探险家兼作家约翰·富兰克林（1786—1847）十四岁加入海军，曾参加特拉法尔加海战。

When peace came, he turned his attention to Arctic exploration, and in particular to solving the conundrum of the Northwest Passage, a mythical clear-water route through the ice which would, if it existed, link the Pacific Ocean on America’s West Coast with the Atlantic on its East.
战事平息后，他转向北极探险，尤其想解开西北航道之谜：相传有一条穿过冰区的无冰水道，能将美洲西岸的太平洋与东岸的大西洋连通。
The first expedition Franklin led to the Arctic was an arduous overland journey lasting from 1819 to 1822, in which he and his twenty-strong team covered 8,880 kilometres on foot.
1819 至 1822 年，他首次率队前往北极，带着约二十人的队伍在艰险的陆路上徒步走了 8,880 公里。

Their expedition was a triumph of surveying – they managed to chart hundreds of kilometres of previously unknown coastline – but food ran out on their journey back to civilisation, and the men were forced to eat their belts and their boots (which they boiled up to make leather soup).
这次考察在测绘上大获成功，探险队绘出了数百公里此前尚未测绘的海岸线，但他们在返回有人定居的地方途中耗尽粮食，只得把皮带和靴子煮成皮汤充饥。
paragraphs.gist: 为寻找沟通两洋的西北航道，富兰克林率队徒步近九千公里，测绘了大片未知海岸，返程断粮时竟靠煮皮具充饥。

sentences: There followed a career as a travel writer and public speaker (‘the man who ate his boots’ was Franklin’s tag-line).
此后他成了游记作家和公众演说家，以「吃过自己靴子的人」闻名。
Then in 1845, Franklin set off back to the Arctic with two ships – the Erebus and the Terror – and 129 men.
1845 年，富兰克林带着 129 人，乘「埃里伯斯号」和「恐怖号」再次驶向北极。
Nothing was heard of them for 14 years, although more than 30 expeditions were dispatched in search of them.
尽管先后派出三十多支探险队搜寻，他们仍有十四年杳无音讯。
Eventually it was discovered that Franklin and all his team had perished after their ships were trapped in the ice.
后来人们才得知，两艘船受困冰中，富兰克林及其队员全部遇难。
paragraphs.gist: 第一次远征后，富兰克林靠写作和演讲为人熟知，1845 年重返北极却音讯全无，搜寻多年才得知全队遇难。

paragraphs.brief: 小说填补史料的性格空白
sentences: In his personal correspondence and published memoirs, Franklin comes across as a man dedicated to the external duties of war and exploration, who kept introspection and self-analysis to a minimum.
从私人信件和公开出版的回忆录看，富兰克林全心履行作战与探险的职责，很少剖析自己的内心。
His blandness makes him an amenably malleable subject for a novelist, and Sten Nadolny has taken full advantage of this in his book.
他留给人的印象平淡，反而给小说家留下了塑造人物的余地，斯滕·纳多尼在书中充分利用了这一点。
Most important, Nadolny has endowed John Franklin with a defining trait for which there is no historical evidence: Langsamkeit (‘slowness’, or ‘calmness’).
最重要的是，纳多尼赋予他一种史无实据的标志性特质：德语所说的 Langsamkeit，即「缓慢」或「从容」。
paragraphs.gist: 富兰克林留下的文字多谈职责，少谈内心，小说家纳多尼便在史料的空白处塑造出一个以「慢」为特点的人物。

paragraphs.brief: 少年富兰克林向往北极的缘由
sentences: Slowness influences not only Franklin’s behaviour, but also his vision, his thought and his speech.
这种慢体现在富兰克林的行为、观察、思考和说话方式中。
The opening scene of The Discovery of Slowness depicts Franklin as a young boy, failing to catch a ball because his reaction time is too slow.
《慢的发现》开篇写少年富兰克林因反应太慢，没能接住球。
Despite the bullying of his peers, Franklin resolves not to fall into step with ‘their way of doing things’.
即使受到同伴欺凌，他也决心不照「他们的方式」行事。
For Nadolny, Franklin’s fascination with the Arctic stems from his desire to find an environment suited to his peculiar slowness.
在纳多尼笔下，富兰克林迷恋北极，是因为他渴望找到适合自己独特节奏的环境。
He describes Franklin as a boy dreaming of the ‘time without hours and days’ which exists in the far north, a place ‘where nobody would find him too slow’.
作者写他儿时梦想着遥远北方那「不分小时与日期的时光」，在那里「没人会嫌他太慢」。
paragraphs.gist: 小说从少年富兰克林慢得接不住球写起，把他对北极的向往解释为渴望找到一个无须按别人节奏生活的地方。

paragraphs.brief: 极地探险为何需要耐心
sentences: Ice is a slow mover.
冰的变化极为缓慢。
The compressed blue ice inside an Alpine crevasse will have fallen as snow several decades earlier.
阿尔卑斯冰川裂隙里压实的蓝冰，几十年前还是落下的雪。
Polar pack ice takes at least two years to form.
极地浮冰至少需要两年才能形成。

The film of crystals which first appears on the surface of the sea thickens into a silkily pliant layer called nilas; this in turn consolidates into young ice, which then deepens during several seasons to become pack.
海面初现的薄薄一层冰晶逐渐增厚，成了丝绸般柔韧的薄冰，再凝结成初生冰，经过几个季节才增厚为浮冰。
Ice demands a corresponding patience from those who venture onto it.
踏上冰面的人也得有与之相称的耐心。
The explorers who have thrived at high latitudes and at high altitudes haven’t usually been men of great speed.
能在高纬度和高海拔地区从容应对挑战的探险家，通常并不以速度见长。
They have tended instead to demonstrate unusual self-possession, a considerable capacity for boredom, and a talent for the uncomplaining endurance of suffering.
他们往往格外镇定，耐得住漫长的单调，也能毫无怨言地忍受痛苦。
paragraphs.gist: 从积雪压成冰川到海冰逐季增厚，冰的变化体现了极地探险对人的要求：能沉住气，耐得住单调与艰辛。

paragraphs.brief: 先想后做赢得水手尊重
sentences: These were all qualities which the historical Franklin possessed in abundance, and so Nadolny’s exaggeration of them isn’t unreasonable.
历史上的富兰克林本就具备这些品质，因此纳多尼将它们加以放大，并非没有道理。

Even as an adult, Franklin’s slowness of thought means that he is unable to speak fluently, so he learns by heart ‘entire fleets of words and batteries of responses’, and speaks a languid, bric-à-brac language.
小说里的富兰克林成年后仍因思考慢而说话磕绊，只好背下「舰队般的词汇、炮阵般的应答」，说起话来慢悠悠的，用语也东拼西凑。
In the Navy, his method of thinking first and acting later initially provokes mockery from his fellow sailors.
在海军中，他先想后做的习惯起初引来其他水手的嘲笑。
But Franklin persists in doing things his way, and gradually earns the respect of those around him.
但他坚持自己的做法，逐渐赢得了身边人的尊重。
To a commodore who tells him to speed up his report of an engagement, he replies: ‘When I tell something, sir, I use my own rhythm.’
一位海军准将催他快点汇报交战经过，他回答：「长官，我说事情有自己的节奏。」
A lieutenant says approvingly of him: ‘Because Franklin is so slow, he never loses time.’
一名海军中尉赞许地说：「正因为富兰克林慢，他从不浪费时间。」
paragraphs.gist: 小说放大了富兰克林本有的沉着，他靠背熟词句克服表达困难，也凭先想后做的习惯赢得原本嘲笑他的水手的尊重。

sentences: Nadolny also brings his central metaphor of slowness to bear on the novel’s language.
纳多尼也把「慢」这个核心隐喻融进小说的语言。
The chapters describing Franklin’s early years are a medley of separate fragments, rhetorical questions, associative jumps and exclamation marks.
描写富兰克林早年的章节交织着零散片段、反问、跳跃的联想和感叹号。
In the later sections recounting Franklin’s first Arctic expedition, Nadolny brilliantly sets the narrative pace to the rhythms of the frozen landscape, and to the ‘slowness which is bred by hunger’.
后面写到首次北极探险时，作者巧妙地让叙事节奏贴合冰原的步调，以及「饥饿孕育的缓慢」。
paragraphs.gist: 纳多尼把「慢」写进叙事节奏：少年时代的章节片段跳跃，写到极地探险时，文字的步调便顺着冰原与饥饿放缓。

paragraphs.brief: 反思高速文化引发广泛共鸣
sentences: Since it was first published in Germany in 1983, The Discovery of Slowness has sold more than a million copies and been translated into 15 languages.
《慢的发现》1983 年在德国首次出版，此后销量超过一百万册，并被译成十五种语言。

It has been adopted as a manual and manifesto by European pressure groups and institutions representing causes as diverse as sustainable development, management science and motoring policy, even becoming involved in the debate about speed limits on German roads.
欧洲一些倡议团体和机构把它当成行动指南和宣言，涉及可持续发展、管理科学和交通政策等领域，甚至在德国公路限速的争论中也有人引用它。
The various groups that have taken the novel up have one thing in common: a dislike of the high-speed culture of Post-modernity.
这些推崇小说的团体有个共同点：都不喜欢后现代社会追求高速的文化。
Nadolny’s Franklin appeals to them because he is immune to ‘the compulsion to be constantly occupied’, and to the idea that ‘someone was better if he could do the same thing fast’.
他们欣赏纳多尼笔下的富兰克林，是因为他不觉得人「必须时刻忙碌」，也不认同「同一件事做得快的人就更优秀」。
It’s easy to see where the attraction lies for those in management.
管理界人士为何会被吸引，也不难理解。
The novel is crammed with quotations about time-efficiency, punctiliousness and profitability: ‘What did “too late” mean?
书里随处可见关于时间效率、一丝不苟和盈利能力的警句，例如：「所谓太晚，到底是什么意思？
They hadn’t waited for it long enough, that’s what it meant.’
意思就是他们等得还不够久。」
paragraphs.gist: 反感事事求快的读者在富兰克林身上看到另一种生活节奏，这也解释了小说为什么会被管理界、环保团体等奉为宣言。

items.en: a summary of Franklin’s occupation in the period before his first expedition
items.zh: 概述富兰克林首次探险前从事的职业
items.why: A 段回顾富兰克林十四岁加入海军并参加特拉法加海战的经历，交代的是他首次探险前的职业生涯。

items.en: a reference to a feature of Franklin’s character in Nadolny’s novel that has no definite basis in fact
items.zh: 指出纳多尼笔下富兰克林的一种性格特征缺乏确切史料依据
items.why: C 段说明小说赋予富兰克林一个标志性特点“缓慢或沉静”，同时明确指出这一特质缺少历史证据。

items.en: a connection between the central theme of the novel and an environmental process
items.zh: 说明小说的核心主题和某种自然过程之间的联系
items.why: E 段以冰的缓慢运动引出冰面对探险者耐心的要求，让自然过程对应小说中“缓慢”这一核心主题。

items.en: a reference to the widespread appeal of Nadolny’s novel
items.zh: 提到纳多尼的小说在不同群体中广受欢迎
items.why: H 段用销量逾百万册、被译成十五种语言说明小说的传播范围，属于其广受欢迎的直接证据。

items.en: a summary of events following Franklin’s return from his first expedition
items.zh: 概述富兰克林首次探险归来后发生的事
items.why: B 段接续首次探险，讲富兰克林回国后写游记、公开演讲和随后的人生经历，正是题干所问的返航后大事概述。

items.en: John Franklin and the Quality of Slowness Little is known from Franklin’s correspondence and published writings about his ________.
items.zh: 从约翰·富兰克林的书信和公开著作中，人们对他的 ________ 所知甚少。
items.why: 书信和与回忆录几乎不提供有关他“个性/人格” 的信息，故选 personality.

items.en: He begins the book by showing how this affects the young Franklin’s ________ activities, and makes him become ____ (Q34).
items.zh: 作者在书的开头写到，这种特质怎样影响少年富兰克林的 ________ 活动，并使他成了 ________（Q34）。
items.why: 描写的正是抓球等“体育活动”,故用 sporting.

items.en: He begins the book by showing how this affects the young Franklin’s ____ (Q33) activities, and makes him become ________.
items.zh: 作者在书的开头写到，这种特质怎样影响少年富兰克林的 ________（Q33） 活动，并使他成了 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“即使受到同伴欺凌，他也决心不照「他们的方式」行事”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: As a child, it is the quality of ________ that attracts Franklin to the Arctic.
items.zh: 童年时，北极的 ________ 特质吸引了富兰克林。
items.why: 回到对应内容“作者写他儿时梦想着遥远北方那「不分小时与日期的时光」，在那里「没人会嫌他太慢」”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

items.en: In paragraph E, the writer describes different types of ice in order to illustrate
items.zh: E 段描写了几种不同的冰，作者想借此说明什么？
correct: the personal qualities required of an explorer in Arctic conditions.
探险者在北极环境中需要具备哪些个人素质。

items.en: What is said about the way Franklin communicates?
items.zh: 文中如何描述富兰克林与人交流的方式？
correct: He uses words and phrases that he has previously memorised.
他使用事先背熟的词句。

items.en: How does the attitude of the other sailors change towards Franklin?
items.zh: 其他水手对富兰克林的态度发生了怎样的变化？
correct: They eventually appreciate his good qualities.
他们最终认识到富兰克林的优点。

items.en: The chapters of The Discovery of Slowness which describe Franklin’s early years contain
items.zh: 《慢的发现》中描述富兰克林早年的章节包含什么？
correct: 许多彼此不连贯的短小片段。

items.en: The Discovery of Slowness has achieved widespread popularity because
items.zh: 《慢的发现》为什么会广受欢迎？
correct: it reflects many people’s concern about one aspect of modern life.
它反映了许多人对现代生活某一方面的担忧。

points: H 段用销量逾百万册、被译成十五种语言说明小说的传播范围，属于其广受欢迎的直接证据。
回到对应内容“作者写他儿时梦想着遥远北方那「不分小时与日期的时光」，在那里「没人会嫌他太慢」”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Nothing was heard of them for 14 years, ….
连接词 although 引出“although more than 30 expeditions were dispatched in search of them”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
“that Franklin and all his team had perished after their ships were trapped in the ice”补足 discovered 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 discovered 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
